text: Emmanuel Dapidran Pacquiao Sr., born December 17, 1978, in Kibawe, Bukidnon, Philippines, is a Filipino professional boxer and retired politician, widely regarded as one of the greatest professional boxers of all time and the only eight-division world champion in boxing history. He won twelve major world titles, including the lineal championship in four weight classes: flyweight, featherweight, super featherweight, and light welterweight. Pacquiao is the first boxer to win major world titles in four of the original eight "glamour divisions" (flyweight, featherweight, lightweight, and welterweight) and the only boxer to hold world championships across four decades (1990s, 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s). In July 2019, he became the oldest welterweight world champion in history at age 40 and the first boxer to become a recognized four-time welterweight champion after defeating Keith Thurman for the WBA (Super) welterweight title. His fights generated $1.2 billion in revenue from 25 pay-per-view bouts, and as of 2015, he earned $1.3 billion from 26 PPV bouts. Forbes ranked him the second highest paid athlete in the world in 2012 and 2015, and the eighth highest paid athlete of the 2010s. In 2024, ESPN ranked him the greatest Asian athlete of the 21st century, and in 2025, The Ring ranked him second among the greatest pound-for-pound fighters of the 21st century. He was inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2025. Pacquiao entered politics in 2010 when elected as representative of Sarangani, serving until 2016 when he became a senator. He became the leader of the ruling PDP–Laban party in 2020 (a position disputed since 2021). On September 19, 2021, he officially declared his candidacy for President of the Philippines in the 2022 election, losing to Bongbong Marcos. After losing the 2025 Senate election, he announced his retirement from politics and came out of retirement from boxing. He was introduced to boxing at age 12 by his maternal uncle Sardo Mejia, and began training in a home gym before fighting in a park in General Santos. At age 16, he made his professional debut in January 1995 as a junior flyweight. He won his first major title, the WBC flyweight title, on December 4, 1998. Over his career, he defeated 22 world champions, including Chatchai Sasakul, Lehlohonolo Ledwaba, Jorge Eliécer Julio, Marco Antonio Barrera (twice), Érik Morales (twice), Óscar Larios, Jorge Solís, Juan Manuel Márquez (twice), David Díaz, Oscar De La Hoya, Ricky Hatton, Miguel Cotto, Joshua Clottey, Antonio Margarito, Shane Mosley, Brandon Ríos, Timothy Bradley (twice), Chris Algieri, Jessie Vargas, Lucas Matthysse, Adrien Broner, and Keith Thurman. His most recent bout was against Mario Barrios in July 2025. He participated in an exhibition match against Jesus Salud in August 2002, which he won. He was named "Fighter of the Decade" for the 2000s by the BWAA, WBC, WBO, The Sporting News, and HBO, and won Ring magazine, ESPN, and BWAA Fighter of the Year in 2006, 2008, and 2009, as well as the Best Fighter ESPY Award in 2009 and 2011. BoxRec ranks him the greatest Asian fighter of all time. In 2016, he ranked No. 2 on ESPN's list of top pound-for-pound boxers of the past 25 years and No. 4 on BoxRec's list of greatest pound-for-pound boxers of all time. As of 2022, he was ranked ninth in The Ring's list of top 100 boxers of all time. In 2025, he was awarded the Fighter of the Century honor by the WBC and joined Sugar Ray Robinson as the only boxer to win the "triple crown" of legacy awards: Fighter of the Year, Fighter of the Decade, and Fighter of the Century. He holds six Guinness World Records, including the most consecutive boxing world title fight victories at different weights (15, between 2005 and 2011), the oldest welterweight world champion (age 40 years 215 days, July 20, 2019), and the most boxing world titles won in different weight divisions (eight, after defeating Antonio Margarito in 2010). He also recorded the highest-selling pay-per-view boxing match in a welterweight title fight on May 2, 2015, at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas, and the highest revenue from ticket sales for a boxing match on that date. Pacquiao never competed in the Summer Olympics but served as flag bearer for the Philippines at the 2008 opening ceremony, the first non-participant to do so. He had the opportunity to compete in the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro but declined. He expressed interest in qualifying for the 2024 Summer Olympics in France, but the Philippine Olympic Committee's petition to the IOC was rejected, and he was disallowed due to the 40-year-old age limit. In 2014, he joined the PBA as player-coach for Kia/Mahindra from 2014 to 2017, becoming the oldest rookie drafted in PBA history (11th overall in 2014). He played briefly in a 2015 game, scoring one point, and made his first field goal in 2015 and a career-high four points with a three-pointer in 2016. In 2017, he founded the semi-professional Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League, which turned professional in 2022. He retired from the MPBL in 2018 after playing ten games and scoring less than fifteen points. In 2019, he announced plans to own an NBA team after boxing retirement. He ran for the House of Representatives in 2007 as a candidate of the Liberal Party faction under Lito Atienza, but was forced to run under the Kabalikat ng Malayang Pilipino (KAMPI) and lost to Darlene Antonino-Custodio. On October 25, 2025, he was appointed vice president of the International Boxing Association, though the Philippine Olympic Committee cautioned him due to the IBA's expulsion from the IOC. He is an Evangelical Christian preacher, philanthropist, and entrepreneur, and has released multiple PARI-certified platinum albums and songs, with his cover of "Sometimes When We Touch" peaking at 19 on Billboard's Adult Contemporary chart after a performance on Jimmy Kimmel Live. He is the fourth of six siblings, one of whom, Alberto "Bobby" Pacquiao, is also a politician and former professional boxer. His parents, Rosalio Pacquiao and Dionisia Dapidran, separated when he was in sixth grade after his father had an affair. He was raised in General Santos, Mindanao, and at age 14 moved to Manila, where he lived on the streets, worked as a construction worker, and had to choose between eating and sending money to his mother. He completed elementary school at Saavedra Saway Elementary School but dropped out of high school due to poverty. In February 2007, he passed a high school equivalency exam and was awarded a diploma by the Department of Education. Boxing historian Bert Sugar ranked him the greatest southpaw fighter of all time, and in 2021, he ranked number 1 in DAZN's list of the top 10 boxers of the last 30 years. He was long rated as the best active boxer in the world, pound for pound, by ESPN, Sports Illustrated, Sporting Life, Yahoo! Sports, About.com, BoxRec, and The Ring, beginning from his climb to lightweight until his losses in 2012. He was the longest reigning top-ten active boxer on The Ring's pound for pound list from 2003 to 2016. He has an amateur record of 60–4 and a professional record of 62–8–3, with 39 wins by knockout. He stated that he became a fighter because he had to survive, with no one to depend on except himself, and that boxing was something he was good at that allowed him to keep himself and his family alive.

Manny Pacquiao officially retired from the league after playing ten games over three seasons and scoring fewer than fifteen career points, with rumors circulating about a transfer to Blackwater. In 2019, he announced plans to own an NBA team after his boxing retirement. On February 12, 2007, he announced his campaign for the Philippine House of Representatives' 1st District of South Cotabato as a candidate of the Liberal Party faction under Manila mayor Lito Atienza, motivated by local officials of General Santos who hoped he would serve as a bridge between their interests and the national government. However, courts forced him to run under the Kabalikat ng Malayang Pilipino (KAMPI), a pro-Arroyo party, and he was defeated by incumbent Rep. Darlene Antonino-Custodio of the Nationalist People's Coalition (NPC), who stated that people were not prepared to lose him as their boxing icon. To prepare for his political career, Pacquiao enrolled in the Certificate Course in Development, Legislation, and Governance at the Development Academy of the Philippines – Graduate School of Public and Development Management (DAP-GSPDM). On November 21, 2009, he announced a run for a congressional seat in Sarangani province, his wife Jinkee’s hometown. In May 2010, he was elected to the House of Representatives in the 15th Congress, winning a landslide over the Chiongbian clan, who had held power in the province for over thirty years; he received 120,052 votes compared to Roy Chiongbian’s 60,899. In 2010, he delivered a speech on human trafficking that earned praise but faced criticism for appearing uninformed during a discussion of the reproductive health bill. In 2013, he was re-elected to the 16th Congress without opposition. His wife Jinkee was elected vice-governor of Sarangani, and his younger brother Rogelio lost his congressional bid. Due to other commitments, Pacquiao attended only one session of the final Congress and was criticized as the top absentee among lawmakers; he filed fewer than 20 bills over six years, with none passing committee. On October 5, 2015, he declared a run for senator under the United Nationalist Alliance (UNA) party led by vice-president Jejomar Binay. On May 19, 2016, he was formally elected senator, receiving over 16 million votes and placing seventh. He previously aligned with the Duterte government, facilitating the ouster of Leila de Lima from the Senate Justice committee chairmanship in September 2016 and criticizing her presentation of an alleged Davao Death Squad member. In another Senate hearing, he defended then-Davao City Vice Mayor Paolo Duterte from allegations involving a 2017 ₱6.4-billion illegal drug shipment from Xiamen, China. As of 2018, he filed 31 Senate bills during the 17th Congress, including one with Senators Bato dela Rosa and Bong Go supporting the return of capital punishment. In June 2019, the Philippine Senate reported Pacquiao had the worst attendance record among senators in the 17th Congress, reflecting a long-standing issue, yet he still enacted four laws from his filed bills. During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, he partnered with Alibaba Group co-founder Jack Ma to deliver 50,000 test kits to the Philippines through their charity foundations. In December 2020, he became acting party president of PDP–Laban after Koko Pimentel resigned, though the position became disputed with Energy Secretary Alfonso Cusi, whose faction voted to remove him on July 17, citing expired term limits; Pacquiao remains party president in his faction. In May 2021, he filed a bill to create the Philippine Boxing and Combat Sports Commission, which was criticized by Senator Pia Cayetano for timing during the pandemic. He had previously filed the bill during the 17th Congress, where he and Senator Franklin Drilon became controversial during an interpellation, with Pacquiao reportedly being coached by advisers. In May 2022, he called for the "speedy release" of Senator Leila De Lima, whose detention had lasted five years, after witnesses against her retracted their testimony; he had previously criticized De Lima’s alleged links to drug lord Kerwin Espinosa. As early as June 2020, his former promoter Bob Arum stated that Pacquiao expressed interest in running in 2022, saying, "Bob, I'm gonna run in 2022 and, when I win, I want you there at my inauguration." In June 2021, he criticized Duterte’s stance on China’s South China Sea claims, prompting Duterte to rebuke him for lacking foreign policy knowledge and challenge him to name corrupt individuals or agencies, threatening a negative campaign in the 2022 elections. After losing his final boxing match against Yordenis Ugas, Pacquiao officially announced his presidential bid on September 19, 2021, during the National Assembly of PDP–Laban organized by his faction. On October 1, he formally registered under the Cebu-based party PROMDI, in alignment with the "MP3 Alliance" between PDP–Laban, PROMDI, and the People's Champ Movement; Cusi then decided he was no longer a member of PDP–Laban. His campaign platforms included fighting corruption and providing nationwide housing for the poor. From February onward, he struggled in presidential polls, ranking fourth to fifth with low ratings, dropping to as low as 1.8 percent in March 2022 (Publicus Asia) and 8 percent (Pulse Asia) with a rising disapproval rating. In March 2022, he challenged frontrunner Bongbong Marcos to a one-on-one debate, criticizing him as "not intelligent enough to be president" and calling those voting for a "plunderer" the "dumbest" in the country. He placed third with roughly four million votes and conceded to Marcos, who won by a landslide. On September 26, 2024, Pacquiao was named a senatorial candidate for the Alyansa para sa Bagong Pilipinas in the 2025 elections under the Partido Federal ng Pilipinas, formalizing his bid by filing his certificate of candidacy on October 7, 2024. He lost the Senate bid, placing 18th out of 12 seats and receiving 10,397,133 votes. He has considered leaving politics after returning to boxing. With rising fame, Pacquiao began an acting and hosting career with guest appearances on ABS-CBN shows, signing a contract with the network shortly after. In December 2005, he took his first lead role in Violett Films' Lisensyadong Kamao (Licensed Fist), a film titled because (according to director Tony Bernal) he is licensed to use his hands. Upon the expiration of his ABS-CBN contract, he signed with GMA Network in September 2007, taping his first episode of Pinoy Records a few months later. Other GMA projects included Totoy Bato and the sitcom Show Me Da Manny, where he appeared with Marian Rivera and his mother Dionisia also appeared; he also hosted Manny Many Prizes. In 2008, he starred in Anak ng Kumander (Child of a Commander) with Ara Mina and Valerie Concepcion, a film that was not a commercial success and was criticized by critics. In 2009, he starred in the superhero/comedy film Wapakman, released on December 25 as a Metro Manila Film Festival entry, which also failed commercially. In 2020, he was cast to portray General Miguel Malvar in the biopic Malvar: Tuloy ang Laban, which received mixed reactions from the Malvar family, with concerns from Gabriel, grandson of General Malvar’s youngest child, that Pacquiao’s fame might overshadow the character, while Villegas, son of Malvar’s daughter, supported the casting. Pacquiao recorded songs for his fight entrances and released them on two albums certified platinum in the Philippines; most of his Tagalog songs were composed by Lito Camo, who wrote his biggest hit, "Para Sayo ang Laban Na 'To." On November 3, 2009, he covered "Sometimes When We Touch" by Dan Hill on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, marking his first American TV singing performance; he returned on March 3, 2010, to cover "Nothing's Gonna Change My Love for You." He later released Dan Hill’s hit in April 2011, which reached number 19 on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart, making him one of the few Southeast Asians to enter a US Billboard chart. He also appeared with Will Ferrell and sang "Imagine" for his third guesting; Canadian rapper Drake created a parody, prompting Pacquiao to post a video of himself singing. In 2015, he released an extended play featuring his entrance song for the Floyd Mayweather Jr. fight and announced his retirement from music, stating, "I love music, but music is not for me." The following are Manny Pacquiao's albums from 2006 to 2015. A film based on his life, Pacquiao: The Movie, was released on June 21, 2006, featuring Jericho Rosales and directed by Joel Lamangan, which flopped at the box office, grossing only ₱4,812,191 (approximately US$99,322). Another film, Kid Kulafu, released on April 15, 2015, featured Buboy Villar as young Manny Pacquiao and dramatized his early boxing life. A documentary titled "Manny," with Liam Neeson as narrator, covered his early life and political career. Pacquiao has appeared as a playable character in the Fight Night boxing video game franchise; the character Paquito in Mobile Legends: Bang Bang was inspired by him, with a skin changing his appearance to resemble the real boxer. Filipino game developer Ranida Games announced in 2021 that a mobile game, Fighting Pride: The Manny Pacquiao Saga, is in development. Pacquiao was named one of Time's 100 most influential people in 2009 for his boxing achievements and influence in the Philippines. He was also included in Forbes’ Celebrity 100 list for 2009, joining Angelina Jolie, Woods, and Bryant. He appeared on the cover of Time magazine Asia in November 16, 2009, where it was noted that he had the charisma, intelligence, and backstory to revive boxing, and that global brands like Nike wanted him in ads. He became the eighth Filipino to appear on the Time cover, following Manuel L. Quezon, Ramon Magsaysay, Ferdinand Marcos, Corazon Aquino, Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, Benigno "Noynoy" Aquino III, and Chin Chin Gutierrez. He was also featured on the cover of Reader's Digest Asia in November 2008, before his fight against De La Hoya. Pacquiao is mentioned in several hip hop tracks, including Kool A.D.'s "Manny Pacquiao," Pitbull's "Get It Started," A$AP Rocky's "Phoenix," Bad Meets Evil and Bruno Mars' "Lighters," Eminem and Skylar Grey's "Asshole," Future's "Never Gon' Lose," Migos' "Chinatown," Nicki Minaj and Ciara's "I'm Legit," Rick Ross's "High Definition," Jelo Acosta's "Just Like Manny P," and Yung Gravy's "Betty." He became the first Filipino athlete to appear on a postage stamp. A video clip of him greeting followers for New Year's Eve became an internet meme. On November 26, 2013, shortly after defeating Brandon Ríos, the Philippine Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) froze all of Pacquiao’s Philippine bank accounts due to alleged failure to pay ₱2.2 billion in taxes from US fight earnings between 2008 and 2009. The next day, the BIR also froze his Philippine properties; Pacquiao presented documents to the press showing income tax payments to the BIR’s US counterpart, the IRS, and a letter from Bob Arum. In April 2017, as a senator, he approached Philippine authorities to settle the case, though the BIR maintained that taxes were due even if paid to the IRS. Year's Eve was used as a meme in the Internet. On November 26, 2013, a few days after Pacquiao's victory over Brandon Ríos, the Philippine Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) issued a freeze order on all of Pacquiao's Philippine bank accounts due to his alleged failure to pay ₱2.2 billion in taxes for earnings from his fights in the United States between 2008 and 2009. The following day, the BIR also froze all of Pacquiao's Philippine properties. Pacquiao presented documents to the press showing the income tax for non-resident alien payments made by his promoter to the BIR's US counterpart, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), as well as a letter from Bob Arum. In April 2017, Pacquiao, now a senator, approached Philippine authorities to settle the case, though the BIR maintained that taxes were due even if all taxes had been paid to the IRS. In February 2016, Pacquiao, in a video statement posted by TV5, described people in same-sex marriages as behaving worse than animals, claiming animals generally do not have same-sex mating, which drew criticism from LGBT celebrities. Pacquiao later apologized, stating that as a Christian he is against same-sex marriage due to Biblical teachings but does not condemn gay people. Nike ended their partnership with Pacquiao, calling his comments abhorrent, and The Grove at Farmers Market in Los Angeles banned him from the shopping mall. In 2021, Paradigm Sports Management, the company Pacquiao signed an exclusive management deal with a year prior, filed a lawsuit against him, alleging bad faith breach of contract for having two management companies negotiate simultaneously for boxing matches. In early May 2023, Orange County Superior Court ruled in favor of Paradigm Sports Management, ordering Pacquiao to pay $5.1 million plus at least $2 million in attorney fees, both with 10 percent annual interest. In August 2024, the verdict was overturned and vacated, as the court found that when signing the contract, Audie Attar did not hold a management license, which is required under California law. Pacquiao married Jinkee Jamora on May 10, 1999. Together, they have five children: Emmanuel Jr. (Jimuel), Michael Stephen, Mary Divine Grace (Princess), Queen Elizabeth (Queenie), and Israel. In 2006, Joanna Rose Bacosa, a KTV receptionist, disclosed her child with Pacquiao, Emmanuel "Eman" Bacosa, born in January 2004. Although Pacquiao initially did not acknowledge him, he was later seen training with Eman, who began boxing and made his professional debut on September 23, 2023, ending in a draw. He dedicated his win against Noel Pangantao on December 15, 2023, to his father. Jimuel, his eldest son with Jinkee, is a professional boxer who made his debut on November 30, 2025, in a majority draw, and is also a model and actor. Michael, his second son, is a rapper with tens of millions of streams and is an incumbent councilor of General Santos. Princess, his first daughter, is a popular YouTube vlogger with millions of subscribers and started the Pacquiao family's YouTube content network, while Queenie, his second daughter, was born in the United States. On May 27, 2024, Mary Divine Grace "Princess" graduated from Brent International School. Pacquiao resides in his hometown of General Santos, South Cotabato, Philippines. As congressman representing the lone district of Sarangani from 2010 to 2016, he officially resided in Kiamba, Sarangani, the hometown of his wife. Upon being elected to the Senate of the Philippines, he returned his official residence to General Santos, as senators are elected nationwide. Pacquiao has a YouTube channel with 990,000 subscribers as of August 2023. The Pacquiao family posts content about their activities on separate YouTube channels, with his daughter Mary and wife Jinkee each having more than one million subscribers, and his sons Jimuel and Michael each having fewer than 600,000. On June 25, 2010, Pacquiao completed a 10-day crash course on Development Legislation and Governance at the Graduate School of Public and Development Management of the Development Academy of the Philippines (DAP). Pacquiao was officially enrolled for two semesters at Notre Dame of Dadiangas University (NDDU) in the Academic Year 2007–2008 under a bachelor's degree in business administration major in marketing management, but did not complete the program and was not granted a degree. From June 8 to 17, 2016, Pacquiao underwent a 9-day Executive Coaching Program crash course conducted by the Development Academy of the Philippines, the Ateneo School of Government, the Asian Institute of Management, and the Philippine Public Safety College after winning a senate seat in 2016. On December 11, 2019, Pacquiao controversially graduated from the University of Makati with a bachelor's degree in political science, majoring in local government administration through the Expanded Tertiary Education Equivalency and Accreditation Program (ETEEAP) of the Philippine Councilors League-Legislative Academy (PCCLA), which allows qualified Filipinos to complete collegiate-level education via informal education. Pacquiao reportedly completed the degree in one year, contrary to earlier reports of three months. Raised Catholic, Pacquiao is currently practicing and preaching Evangelical Protestantism. He said he once had a dream where he saw a pair of angels and heard the voice of God—this dream convinced him to become a devout believer. Pacquiao enlisted as a military reservist and was promoted to the rank of colonel in the Reserve Force of the Philippine Army. Prior to being promoted to full colonel after completing his General Staff Course (GSC) schooling, he held the rank of lieutenant colonel as a member of the Philippine Congress per AFP regulations. He first entered the army's reserve force on April 27, 2006, as a sergeant. He rose to Technical Sergeant on December 1 of the same year. On October 7, 2007, he became a Master Sergeant, the highest rank for enlisted personnel. On May 4, 2009, he was given the special rank of Senior Master Sergeant and was designated as the Command Sergeant Major of the 15th Ready Reserve Division. In 2022, Pacquiao graduated from Philippine Christian University with a master's degree in management, majoring in public administration. Pacquiao's cousin is Rene Pacquiao, a 6'5 center from Bukidnon, who became a teammate of Pacquiao in the Mahindra Floodbusters. Correct as of February 18, 2018. Correct as of February 2, 2019.
